# Sharpening stones

A pair of whetstones, coarse and fine, soaked in water for ten minutes before use. Hold the blade at about fifteen degrees and push it across the stone in even strokes, ten on each side, then move to the fine grit. A burr on the edge means the angle is right. Finish by stropping on a leather belt.

The same routine works for kitchen knives and for the garden tools; see [[Pruning fruit trees]] for the secateurs. Wipe the steel dry and oil the blades of the garden tools before storing them in the shed for winter.

Do it monthly, not when the edge is already dull.
